findings.text: the mark write was changed here to call pending_landing.mark_pending_landing_repair, but this file is in neither the plan's section-6 write paths nor the dispatch fence, so the node wrote outside its exclusive scope without requesting a scope extension; the change itself is correct and the two tests that reach this line (tests/test_a_conflicting_landing_is_repaired.py, tests/test_a_repair_has_one_path.py) assert individual pointer keys rather than whole-pointer equality, so the added pending_landing_repair_attempt field does not break them, but the remedy is a scope grant recorded by the coordinator rather than a repair to the code.

the retargeted-mark case fails at the base revision with AttributeError on pending_landing.pointer_attempt rather than by releasing the newer pointer, so the manifest's negative_control_note claim that the retargeted-mark case fails at base holds only in the sense that a symbol the change introduces is absent; the behavioural reading for that case is the deliberate one at the head, and the base arm does not demonstrate the pointer loss it is credited with there.
